description: Retail demo data catalog: tables, columns, types, keys, relationships and meanings. Generated by retail.export_catalog; do not edit by hand.

countries.name: countries
countries.description: Countries where customers, stores, warehouses or suppliers are located.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Country name in English, for example 'United States'.

columns.name: iso_code
columns.description: Two-letter ISO 3166 country code, for example 'US'.

regions.name: regions
regions.description: Sales regions the company reports on.

stores.name: stores
stores.description: Physical stores. Store sales appear in orders with channel 'store'.
caveats: Boulder Basecamp opened on 1 July 2025; it has no sales before that date, so compare stores over periods when all were open.

warehouses.name: warehouses
warehouses.description: Distribution centres that ship online orders and hold stock.

brands.name: brands
brands.description: Brands the company sells, including its own private label.

columns.name: is_private_label
columns.description: True for the company's own brand (Trailhead Essentials).

categories.name: categories
categories.description: Product category tree. Top-level categories (Camping, Hiking, Apparel, Climbing, Accessories) have no parent; some branches go three levels deep (Apparel > Jackets > Rain Jackets).
caveats: Products sit in the lowest category. To total a top-level category, walk up parent_id (a recursive WITH query, or join categories to itself).

columns.name: name
columns.description: Category name, for example 'Tents' or 'Rain Jackets'.

columns.name: parent_id
columns.description: Parent category; empty for a top-level category.

product_prices.name: product_prices
product_prices.description: List price history of each product.
product_prices.grain: One row per product per price period.
caveats: Periods are contiguous: valid_to of one row equals valid_from of the next. The current price has an empty valid_to.
The price on a given date is the row where valid_from <= date < valid_to (or valid_to is empty).

columns.name: valid_to
columns.description: First day it no longer applied; empty for the current price.

product_suppliers.name: product_suppliers
product_suppliers.description: Which suppliers can supply each product, at what cost and lead time.
product_suppliers.grain: One row per product and supplier.

columns.name: unit_cost
columns.description: Purchase cost per unit from this supplier.

columns.name: lead_time_days
columns.description: Usual days from purchase order to delivery.

columns.name: is_primary
columns.description: True for the supplier normally used for this product.

products.name: products
products.description: Products in the range, past and present.
caveats: The current price is not on this table; it is in product_prices. For what customers paid, use order_items.unit_price.

columns.name: unit_cost
columns.description: What one unit costs the company to buy.

columns.name: launched_on
columns.description: Date the product went on sale.

columns.name: discontinued_on
columns.description: Date the product stopped being sold; empty if still on sale. The Ridgeline 300 Headlamp was discontinued on 10 June 2025 after a recall.

suppliers.name: suppliers
suppliers.description: Companies the products are bought from.

columns.name: country_id
columns.description: Country the supplier is based in.

customer_addresses.name: customer_addresses
customer_addresses.description: Shipping and billing addresses of customers.

columns.name: address_type
columns.description: What the address is used for.

columns.name: is_default
columns.description: True for the customer's default address.

customers.name: customers
customers.description: Registered customers. Guest checkouts are not customers (orders.customer_id is empty for them).

columns.name: birth_year
columns.description: Year of birth; empty when not given.

columns.name: acquisition_channel
columns.description: How the customer first found the company.

columns.name: marketing_opt_in
columns.description: True if the customer agreed to marketing email.

loyalty_memberships.name: loyalty_memberships
loyalty_memberships.description: Loyalty tier history of each customer.
loyalty_memberships.grain: One row per customer per tier period.
caveats: A customer's current tier is the row with an empty valid_to. Some customers moved up a tier, so they have an earlier row too; filter on valid_to IS NULL to count members per tier.

columns.name: valid_to
columns.description: First day no longer in the tier; empty if current.

columns.name: min_annual_spend
columns.description: Yearly spend that qualifies for the tier.

columns.name: discount_pct
columns.description: Member discount applied to every order.

order_items.name: order_items
order_items.description: Products on each order, with the price actually paid.
order_items.grain: One row per product on an order.
caveats: unit_price is the price paid on the order date; it can differ from the current list price in product_prices.
line_total = quantity * unit_price - discount_amount. Product revenue is SUM(line_total) for completed orders.

columns.name: unit_price
columns.description: List price of one unit on the order date.

columns.name: discount_amount
columns.description: Promotion and loyalty discount on the line.

columns.name: line_total
columns.description: What the customer paid for the line: quantity * unit_price - discount_amount.

order_promotions.name: order_promotions
order_promotions.description: Which promotion codes were used on which orders.
order_promotions.grain: One row per order and promotion.

orders.name: orders
orders.description: Customer orders, online and in stores, January 2024 to September 2026.
caveats: Revenue counts completed orders only: filter status = 'completed'. Cancelled orders stay in the table.
Order totals are already summed from their items. Never SUM(orders.total_amount) after joining order_items: each order would be counted once per item.
Guest checkouts have an empty customer_id; an inner join to customers drops them. Use a LEFT JOIN when counting all orders.
Store orders have a store_id and no shipping; online orders have no store_id.
Returns are not subtracted here; they are in returns, per item.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: Customer who placed the order; empty for guest checkouts.

columns.name: store_id
columns.description: Store for store orders; empty for online orders.

columns.name: shipping_address_id
columns.description: Delivery address for online orders of registered customers.

columns.name: ordered_at
columns.description: When the order was placed (store local time).

columns.name: subtotal
columns.description: Sum of quantity times unit price over the items, before discounts.

columns.name: shipping_fee
columns.description: Shipping charged to the customer; 0 for store orders and online orders of 100 or more.

payments.name: payments
payments.description: Payments taken for orders. A few orders are split between a gift card and another method.
caveats: Cancelled orders have a refunded payment; captured payments add up to the order total for completed orders.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Promotion name, for example 'Spring Trail Sale'.

returns.name: returns
returns.description: Items customers sent back, with the refund paid.
returns.grain: One row per return of an order line.
caveats: Net revenue = SUM(order_items.line_total) for completed orders minus SUM(returns.refund_amount) for those items.

columns.name: reason
columns.description: Why it was returned. 'recall' is the Ridgeline 300 Headlamp recall of June 2025.

shipments.name: shipments
shipments.description: Deliveries of completed online orders from a warehouse.

columns.name: delivered_at
columns.description: When it was delivered; empty if still in transit or lost.

columns.name: shipping_cost
columns.description: What the delivery cost the company.

inventory_snapshots.name: inventory_snapshots
inventory_snapshots.description: Stock levels per product and warehouse, taken every Monday.
inventory_snapshots.grain: One row per Monday, warehouse and product on sale.
caveats: Stock is a level, not a flow: average or take the latest snapshot, never sum snapshots over weeks.

columns.name: quantity_on_order
columns.description: Units ordered from suppliers but not yet received.

purchase_order_items.name: purchase_order_items
purchase_order_items.grain: One row per product on a purchase order.

purchase_orders.name: purchase_orders
purchase_orders.description: Orders the company places with suppliers to restock warehouses.
caveats: Delivery delay in days is received_on - expected_on; empty received_on means not yet delivered.

columns.name: received_on
columns.description: Date it was received; empty if open.

campaigns.name: campaigns
campaigns.description: Marketing campaigns that drive visits to the website.

columns.name: order_id
columns.description: Order the ticket is about; empty for account questions.

columns.name: closed_at
columns.description: When it was resolved; empty if still open.

columns.name: satisfaction_score
columns.description: Customer rating after closing; empty if not given.

web_sessions.name: web_sessions
caveats: A visit that ended in a purchase has an order_id. Conversion rate = visits with an order_id / all visits.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: Signed-in customer; empty for anonymous visits.

columns.name: campaign_id
columns.description: Campaign the visit came from; empty if none.

columns.name: order_id
columns.description: Order placed during the visit; empty if none.

employees.name: employees
employees.description: Employees, at headquarters and in stores.
caveats: manager_id points to another employee; the chief executive has none. Use a recursive WITH query to walk the reporting line.

columns.name: store_id
columns.description: Store for store staff; empty for headquarters.
